correctness.rationale: The collision probability is reconstructed exactly from the law of the two-coin difference and the background autocorrelations. Its fixed-sum dependence on the Bernoulli product is a quadratic with positive coefficient D, where D is half the squared l2 norm of the background second difference. The feasible product interval is exact, so projection yields the global optimizer. The two-coin thresholds follow from exact polynomial comparisons.

value.rationale: Rényi order two is a canonical collision statistic and was explicitly singled out in the generalized Shepp--Olkin literature. The result turns the qualitative transverse instability into a complete global fixed-sum phase diagram and gives an exact reusable pair-transfer criterion with an arbitrary Bernoulli-sum background. The deterministic, unequal, and balanced phases are mathematically distinct and separated by sharp natural thresholds.
